newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco expects San Antonio study mid-Jan - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Codelco expects San Antonio study mid-Jan - CEO.

text.p: Chilean state copper company Codelco expects to receive a preliminary study in mid-January on the San Antonio copper deposit which lies close to its Salvador pit, said CEO Marcos Lima.
"The analysis of the project should be ready mid-January," Lima told reporters.
The study was due this month but was delayed because the corporation's geologists were carrying out extra metallurgical tests, he explained.
Initial studies revealed that the deposit is small by Codelco's standards, with annual production of less than 100,000 tonnes of copper, said Lima.
"The deposit is attractive but we don't think it is the size of Radomiro Tomic or world class," he said, referring to Codelco's 150,000-tonne Radomiro Tomic pit which will start operating next year.
Like Radomiro Tomic, San Antonio has oxide and secondary sulphide reserves which can be treated using new low-cost heap-leaching technology, said Lima.
Codelco will hold a public discussion on ways to fund the San Antonio mine before carrying out a pre-feasibility study, Lima said.
Low-risk projects like San Antonio, which have known reserves, could prove attractive to Chilean companies looking to move into copper mining industry, he added.
Companies which have shown interest in the deposit include industrial conglomerate Compaa de Petrleos de Chile SA (Copec) and local pension funds.
"Copec could perfectly be within the list of potential investors," said Lima.
